# External language worker status

This directory is an admission placeholder, not an executable implementation. It contributes only an empty CMake interface target. EOS currently admits packaged C/C++ ABI v2 skills in `eos-skill-worker`; it does not admit Python skills or launch an interpreter for package code.

Python support needs a distinct C++ `PythonWorkerProvider` and worker bootstrap. Static package metadata and schemas must be validated before any skill module is imported. The provider must use the existing versioned worker IPC and Broker grants; it must not put Python in `eosd`, IsOS, or the native ABI loader. A pybind11 extension inside the isolated worker should expose only the brokered skill execution API, with no raw EOS pointers, file descriptors, or hardware handles.

The current worker cannot host this safely: it discovers only ABI v2 libraries, applies a fixed Landlock allowlist that excludes arbitrary uv/Conda environments, and installs seccomp rules that deny interpreter exec and child creation. The installed `EOS::SkillSDK` reports/checks ABI layout; it is not a reusable broker protocol client. Do not remove those controls or dynamically import package code to work around the missing provider.

The planned worker must default to Python 3.12 while accepting a configured interpreter from an explicit executable, uv environment, or Conda environment. Its C++ bootstrap must authenticate the inherited `SOCK_SEQPACKET` channel, set `no_new_privs` and resource limits, allow read-only access only to the selected interpreter/runtime and admitted package, start Python in isolated mode without site initialization, initialize the trusted pybind11 bridge, install the final syscall policy, and only then import the admitted entry point. The selected runtime and its native libraries are part of the host trust configuration. Worker cancellation, broker revocation, peer credentials, no-network policy, and termination must retain the current fail-closed semantics.

Admission remains open until the Python package descriptor, metadata validation, provider registration, interpreter policy, sandbox bootstrap, and cross-runtime tests land together. Release qualification must cover Python 3.12, a uv environment and a Conda environment, malformed descriptors, denied undeclared capabilities, cancellation during a capability call, worker crash, peer mismatch, and unavailable sandbox features.

See [skill authoring](../../../../../docs/eos/interfaces/skills/native/README.md) and the [external runtime boundary](../../../../../docs/eos/design/runtime/skills/external.md) for the current native worker and the bounded Python admission plan.
